ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, $O$ is a point on line $AC$, $OB$ is a ray, $OD$ bisects $\angle AOB$, $OE$ is within $\angle BOC$, $\angle BOE = \frac{1}{3}\angle EOC$, $\angle DOE = 60^\circ$, then what is the degree measure of $\angle EOC$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Let $\angle BOE$ be $x^\circ$, then $\angle DOB = 60^\circ - x^\circ$,\\
since $\angle BOE = \frac{1}{3}\angle EOC$,\\
it follows that $\angle EOC = 3\angle BOE = 3x^\circ$,\\
given that OD bisects $\angle AOB$,\\
we get $\angle AOB = 2\angle DOB$,\\
thus, we have $3x + x + 2(60 - x) = 180$,\\
solving the equation, we find $x = 30^\circ$,\\
therefore, $\angle EOC = \boxed{90^\circ}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, AC is a horizontal straight line passing through O, with A on the left and C on the right. From point O, three rays are drawn upward: OD is at the upper left and relatively close to OA, OB is between OD and OE, and OE is approximately vertically upward; therefore, going from OA on the left side to OC on the right side, one passes through OD, OB, and OE in order. Reasoning: Let ∠BOE = x°. According to the problem, ∠BOE = (1/3)∠EOC, so ∠EOC = 3x°. In the figure, B is between D and E, and ∠DOE = 60°, therefore ∠DOB = ∠DOE - ∠BOE = 60° - x°. Also because OD bisects ∠AOB, ∠AOD = ∠DOB = 60° - x°, hence ∠AOB = 2(60° - x°). Since AC is a straight line, ∠AOC = 180°, and it is composed of ∠AOD, ∠DOB, ∠BOE, and ∠EOC, so 2(60 - x) + x + 3x = 180. Simplifying gives 120 - 2x + 4x = 180, that is, 2x = 60, therefore x = 30. Therefore ∠EOC = 3x = 90°.
